results.name: Skater Hops
instructions: Stand on one leg with a slight bend in the knee.
Leap sideways and land softly on the other leg.
Swing the free leg behind you and touch the floor lightly, or keep it lifted.
Leap back to the other side and keep alternating.
tips: Land softly and stick each landing.
Swing your arms across your body for momentum.
results.description: Skater Hops is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the glutes (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Abductors, Calves, Core.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Alternating Arm Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles above you with both hands.
Begin by pulling one handle down towards your hip by extending your elbow downward.
Alternate the movement by pulling the opposite handle down towards your hip while bending the other arm upward, mimicking a skiing motion.
Continue alternating the arm pull movements at a steady pace. Repeat for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Adjust the resistance level if needed to provide a challenging but manageable workout.
Use a full range of motion with the handles to engage your upper body muscles effectively.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Alternating Arm Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Arms, Core.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Basic Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands.
Begin by pulling both handles down towards your thighs simultaneously, extending your elbows while pushing your hips back, bending your knees, and leaning your torso forward.
Bring your arms back up to the starting position in a controlled manner.
Continue pulling the handles down at a consistent pace for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on using both your arms and legs to distribute the effort evenly and delay fatigue.
Adjust the resistance level if needed to provide a challenging but manageable workout.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Basic Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Arms, Core.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Face Biceps Curl Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands, palms facing each other. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Begin by pulling both handles towards your face in a curl motion, bending your elbows, and keeping your upper arms stationary.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the handles reach close to your face.
Extend your arms back to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm. Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension on the muscles.
Use a weight or resistance level that provides enough challenge without compromising form.
Keep your upper arms stationary and avoid using your shoulders to lift the handles.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Face Biceps Curl Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Flyes
instructions: Stand with your back facing the ski ergometer machine, feet shoulder-width apart. Hold the handles with both hands. Arms extended out to the sides at shoulder height.
Begin by pulling both handles inward towards each other in a fly motion, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and squeezing your chest muscles as your hands come together.
Pause briefly when the handles are close together in front of your chest, ensuring a strong contraction.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm. Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows to reduce strain on your joints.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension in the muscles.
Focus on engaging your chest muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Flyes is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Core.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Jump Squat Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Begin by pulling both handles down towards your hips while simultaneously lowering into a squat position, bending your knees, and pushing your hips back.
Explosively jump up from the squat position, extending your legs fully while pulling the handles back up in a controlled manner.
Land softly back into the squat position with control, immediately transitioning into the next repetition. Repeat for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement with control, focusing on a smooth transition between the squat and jump to maximize efficiency and reduce injury risk.
Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the exercise.
Focus on using both your arms and legs to distribute the effort evenly and prevent fatigue.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Jump Squat Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Upper Back.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Kneeling Reverse Fly Pull
instructions: Kneel on the floor facing the ski ergometer machine, holding opposite handles with cables crossing, arms extended forward at head height. Engage your core and keep your back straight.
Begin by pulling both handles outward in a reverse fly motion, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together as your arms move out to your sides.
Pause for a second when your arms are fully extended to the sides and slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles outward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Use a resistance level that provides enough challenge without compromising form.
Focus on engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Kneeling Reverse Fly Pull is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Core, Arms.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Pullover Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands and arms straight. Slightly bend your knees, push your hips back, and lean slightly forward.
Begin by pulling both handles down and back in a pullover motion, keeping your arms straight.
Pull the handles down until they are at hip level, then slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles down and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Use a resistance level that provides enough challenge without compromising form.
Keep your arms straight but avoid locking your elbows.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Pullover Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Core, Arms.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Fly Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding opposite handles with cables crossing. Extend your arms forward at head height.
Begin by pulling both handles outward in a reverse fly motion, keeping a slight bend in your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together as your arms move out to your sides.
Pause for a second when your arms are fully extended to the sides and slowly return your arms to the starting position with control, maintaining a steady rhythm.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles outward and inhale as you return them to the starting position.
Use a resistance level that provides enough challenge without compromising form.
Focus on engaging your upper back and shoulder muscles throughout the movement.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Fly Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Core, Arms.

results.name: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Lunge Pull
instructions: Stand in front of the ski ergometer machine with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with both hands. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.

Begin by stepping your right foot back into a reverse lunge position, lowering your body until your right knee is close to the floor and your left thigh is parallel to the floor. Simultaneously, pull both handles down towards your hips.

Pause briefly at the bottom of the lunge, then push through your left heel to return to the starting position, extending your left leg and bringing your right foot forward. Extend your arms back up in a controlled manner.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
tips: Keep your front knee in line with your toes to avoid unnecessary strain.
Maintain a steady pace to ensure consistent tension in the muscles.
Exhale as you pull the handles down and step back into the lunge; inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Ski Ergometer Cross Country Ski Reverse Lunge Pull is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a skierg machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Hamstrings, Core.
